root_cause.text: `mvpp2_bm_switch_buffers()` in the Marvell mvpp2 Ethernet driver unconditionally updated CM3-based TX flow control via `mvpp2_bm_pool_update_priv_fc()` during buffer-pool mode switches, even when `priv->cm3_base` was absent and `priv->global_tx_fc` was false, leading to a NULL-pointer dereference in `mvpp2_cm3_read()/write()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says `mvpp2_bm_switch_buffers()` “unconditionally calls mvpp2_bm_pool_update_priv_fc()” and that this function “programs CM3 flow control registers via mvpp2_cm3_read()/mvpp2_cm3_write(), which dereference priv->cm3_base without any NULL check”; the patch fixes this by changing both calls to `if (change_percpu && priv->global_tx_fc) mvpp2_bm_pool_update_priv_fc(...)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict private flow-control pool updates to cases where global TX flow control is enabled.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding the call to `mvpp2_bm_pool_update_priv_fc(priv, false);` was changed from `if (change_percpu)` to `if (change_percpu && priv->global_tx_fc)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the private flow-control update is now performed only when both `change_percpu` is true and global TX flow control is enabled, preventing that update from running in configurations where global TX flow control is disabled.
